solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: City emptied by Conservative cuts gets me

indicators.note: a word that has been emptied loses its insides, leaving just its outside pair

parts.note: first and last letters of City
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A grumble that Tory spending cuts have hollowed out a city and now hit the writer too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the setter, who signs these puzzles as Cyclops in Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter speaking of themself uses 'me', and this setter's pseudonym is the one-eyed giant's name.

clue.text: Bending end of fanny injured Di in leg

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so these letters are knocked out of shape
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

explanation.surface: Someone called Di is hurt in the leg while bending at the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins the fodder rather than signalling an insertion. Fanny is British slang for genitals, American for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yielding gives way under pressure, so it is bending or flexible.

clue.text: Says "thin" not "sin"? Lost — then piss off!

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports tables

explanation.surface: Someone who mispronounces a word is told to get lost and push off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss off' reads as a rude dismissal; only 'piss' is fodder and 'off' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp turns an s sound into a th, so one who lisps utters 'thin' for 'sin'.

clue.text: Live-in lover? Boring idiot endlessly after a bit!

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a part is a bit of something
a nerd is a dull, socially inept person

explanation.surface: A complaint that a live-in lover is a tedious fool who drones on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for the boring idiot loses its last letter and is placed after the word for a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is the person one lives with in a committed relationship, often unmarried.

clue.text: Dicky swallows unknown quantity every year (evidence of well-developed male)

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside, so the following letters go within

parts.note: p.a. is per annum, every year

explanation.surface: A man feeling dicky keeps downing something yearly, while his torso shows off a fine physique.
explanation.walkthrough: SICK takes in X and PA together. 'Dicky' is British for feeling unwell, and the clue's brackets hold the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pack is a set of visibly defined stomach muscles, a sign of a muscular, well-toned man.

clue.text: Prone to tangle with WI, Cameron would prefer to be completely so

definitions.text: Cameron would prefer to be completely so

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted together out of order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: David Cameron is inclined to clash with the Women's Institute, who famously slow-handclapped a Labour PM.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2010 Cameron governed in coalition with the Lib Dems, so he was only partly in office on his own terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading a coalition, Cameron held office jointly; he would prefer to govern with a full majority of his own.

clue.text: Dick secretly in demand by women who have this?

definitions.text: Dick secretly in demand by women who have this?

parts.words: Dick secretly in demand by women
parts.note: surface reading: women quietly wanting a man's member
setter's reading: the clue describes the Freudian condition named for that wish

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the term Freud coined for girls' supposed wish for male genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory, the condition is a woman's unconscious jealousy of the male organ.

clue.text: Boner gets Willy out of bed

parts.note: someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: An erection gets a man's member up and about in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boner' looks like an erection but is the American word for a blunder; willy is British slang for penis.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-up is a British term for a bungled mistake, just as a boner is a howler.

clue.text: Cameron's 'baby' article on large group dismissed by Thatcher

parts.note: Thatcher said there was no such thing as society

explanation.surface: Cameron's pet project is set against Thatcher's famous dismissal of a large collective.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron's 2010 flagship policy was a slogan of volunteering, while Thatcher said in 1987 that there is no such thing as society.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Society was David Cameron's signature idea, a project he fathered and championed like a baby.

clue.text: Cutting procedure develops his penis — cor, I should go!

indicators.note: something that develops changes its form, so these letters are rearranged
the letter I is told to leave, so one of them is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A boast about some surgery that enlarged a man's member, cut short by a coy request to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from HIS PENIS COR, then rearrange the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship cuts material from publications or films, so it is a procedure of cutting, here with a surgical double meaning.

clue.text: Can Clegg …

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the first name of Clegg, then Lib Dem leader and deputy prime minister

explanation.surface: Read with the next clue, it asks whether the coalition's Clegg can do something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 12-across, so 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning jail. Nick Clegg was the Lib Dem deputy prime minister in the coalition with Cameron.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'nick' and 'can' are British slang for a jail, and Nick is Clegg's forename.

clue.text: … an inventive sort, move 'onside'?

indicators.note: to move things about puts them in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 11-across, it asks whether Clegg, an inventive type, can get himself onside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inventive' looks like praise of Clegg, but it points to a famous inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Report of bollocks on display is very critical

definitions.note: a verb phrase: bawls out means scolds loudly

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: bollocks are balls, and on display is out

explanation.surface: A news story about someone's exposed genitals draws a scathing response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bollocks' is British slang for testicles, as well as for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl someone out is to reprimand them angrily, which is being very critical of them.

clue.text: Superior type of prick, having opening replaced

indicators.note: the opening is the first letter, and replacing it swaps in a different one

parts.note: knob is slang for a prick

explanation.surface: A sneer at a haughty sort of prick who has had an opening replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOB loses its first letter K and takes S in its place; the clue does not say which letter, so the definition decides.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob regards themself as superior to others in class or taste.

clue.text: Pissed Brenda takes right honourable's rear for a source of booze

indicators.note: pissed means drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger out of order

parts.note: Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: 'rear' keeps only the last letter of 'honourable'

explanation.surface: A drunk Brenda chases a Right Honourable's bottom in pursuit of more drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brenda' is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; 'pissed' is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks over a bar, so is the person who supplies the booze.

clue.text: Shagging 'goer' stupid is welcomed by band

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so these letters go within the next word
stupid suggests muddled thinking, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: first part of RING, a band

explanation.surface: Gossip about a dim, promiscuous woman bedding members of a band.
explanation.walkthrough: A goer is British slang for a sexually eager person; the rearranged letters sit inside RING, a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogering is British slang for having sex with someone, a synonym of shagging.

clue.text: So, not at a loss as to where to put your balls, when at table?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having made a profit

definitions.text: where to put your balls, when at table
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the aim at a snooker or pool table, to sink balls in the pockets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' and 'not at a loss' tempt a rude reading; the table is a snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in pocket means to have gained money, and potted balls end up in the table's pockets.

clue.text: Leader of nuts, so wine and dine at others' expense

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a cryptic one: what the testicles lead to is the release of their contents

definitions.text: wine and dine at others' expense
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to live on others' hospitality without paying

explanation.surface: Someone cracked enough to lead the nutters lives it up at other people's cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a rude cryptic reading, a 'free load' as the release the nuts lead to; the second half is the plain definition and carries the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeload is to take food, drink or lodging provided by others without paying anything back.

clue.text: Drug unavailable, reportedly, so relax

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: E is ecstasy, and off means no longer available

explanation.surface: No drugs to be had, so everyone may as well chill out.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for the drug ecstasy; on a menu, a dish that is off has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken effort or tension, which is to relax.

clue.text: Prison shit takes a long time

explanation.surface: Using the toilet in jail is a drawn-out ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle, a place to hold prisoners.

clue.text: American shaggy creature penetrated by penis, centrally

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed inside it

parts.note: the yak is a long-haired ox

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle of the word, so only its central letter is kept

explanation.surface: A lewd tale of an American and a shaggy beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is an informal word for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Function like Labour MPs in Westminster, mate, with sex curtailed

definitions.text: Function like Labour MPs in Westminster

indicators.note: something curtailed is cut short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague

explanation.surface: Labour MPs, mates in the Commons, have their sex lives cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2010 Labour was in opposition at Westminster, against the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: The official opposition's job in Parliament is to resist and challenge the government's measures.

clue.text: Fancy a pisser hosting Kelvin's Klosters entertainment?

indicators.note: a host holds a guest within, so the following letter goes inside
fancy means elaborate or reimagined, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: first part of a pisser rearranged
K is the symbol for kelvin
last letter of a pisser rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to an evening in a Swiss resort with a heavy drinker called Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: Klosters is a Swiss ski resort favoured by the British royals.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the drinking and socialising at a ski resort after the day's skiing.

clue.text: Pisspoor Bob eats crud

indicators.note: what eats something holds it inside, so the next word goes within

parts.note: a nod is a bob of the head

explanation.surface: A mocking verdict on a man named Bob whose diet is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is a brief downward motion of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisspoor is crude slang for very bad, of very low quality, which is what 'no good' means.

clue.text: see 26ac.
(& 25dn.) His organ is handled by many — God! A very small one!

definitions.text: His organ is handled by many

parts.note: a gnome is a tiny folk creature

explanation.surface: A smutty exclamation about a man whose organ many people handle, and how small it turns out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's mythical proprietor, and his 'organ' is the magazine itself, handled by many readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ means a periodical publication; Private Eye's fictional owner is styled as the press baron of that newspaper.

clue.text: In difficulties? Not he, twirling balls

indicators.note: twirling spins things round, so these letters end up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone denies being in trouble while fiddling with his testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage or business on the rocks is failing, so the phrase is an idiom for being in serious trouble.

clue.text: Become less intense when wife takes organ away

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Passion fades once a wife removes her husband's member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' points the surface at a penis; here it is merely the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: When an effect or feeling wears off it gradually fades and loses strength.

clue.text: Government enterprise stifles political understanding

indicators.note: what is stifled is smothered inside, so the letters are held within the phrase before it

parts.note: lies inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A state-run business muffles cross-party agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly accord between countries, as in the Entente Cordiale of Britain and France.
